WebGPUAudioDownmixAlgorithmHelp: Used by the WebGPU player only when the audio destination cannot present the complete 5.1 or 7.1 speaker layout.
WebGPUAudioDownmixStatusLive: Downmix gains applied live and saved for the active WebGPU stereo downmix.
WebGPUAudioDownmixStatusPending: Saved. No active compatible WebGPU stereo downmix accepted the live gain change; the gains will apply to the next compatible client-decoded downmix.
WebGPUAudioLayoutStatusApplying: Switching the active WebGPU client-decoded audio...
WebGPUAudioLayoutStatusLive: Applied to the active WebGPU client-decoded audio; audio pauses briefly while it switches.
WebGPUAudioLayoutStatusPending: No active WebGPU client-decoded audio; it applies to the next client-decoded playback.
WebGPUAudioOutputDescription: System default follows operating-system output changes. Already permitted outputs can be selected directly; Choose output requests browser access when that API is available.
WebGPUAudioOutputPickerUnavailable: This browser does not expose the audio output picker
WebGPUAudioOutputPickerUnavailableHelp: The browser output picker is unavailable; already permitted outputs remain usable.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusDefaultActive: Using the system default audio output.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusDefaultEnumeratio: Available outputs could not be refreshed; playback remains on the system default output.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusDefaultFallback: The system default could not be applied; using one permitted fallback.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusDefaultSaved: The system default audio output is saved for the next active playback path.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusPickerCancelled: Audio output selection was cancelled. Playback output was not changed.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusPickerFailed: The browser could not choose an audio output. Playback output was not changed.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusPickerInvalidDevi: The browser returned an invalid audio output device.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusPickerNotAllowed: Audio output selection is blocked by browser permission or policy.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusPickerNotFound: No audio output device is currently available.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusPickerUnavailable: This browser cannot authorize additional audio outputs. Already permitted outputs can still be selected.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusPickerUserActionR: Choose output must be opened directly from a user action.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusRouteFailed: The requested audio output could not be applied. Playback remains on its current or system-default output.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusSelectedEnumerati: Available outputs could not be refreshed; the selected output remains active and will be retried for new playback paths.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusSelectedFallback: The selected output could not be applied to every active audio path; using a safe fallback.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusSelectedSaved: The selected audio output is saved for the next active playback path.
WebGPUAudioOutputStatusSelectedUnavailab: The saved output is unavailable; using the system default. It will be restored when available.
The saved output and system default are unavailable; using one permitted fallback. The saved output will still be retried.
WebGPUAudioSettingsApplyHelp: Downmix gain changes apply live to an active compatible WebGPU stereo downmix. Speaker layout, force stereo, and downmix algorithm changes switch active client-decoded audio in place, with a brief pause in sound; a binaural change that keeps the layout applies without one.
WebGPUAuthorizeAudioOutput: Authorize an audio output through the browser
WebGPUBinauralHeadphonesHelp: Renders Dolby Atmos objects for headphones when WebGPU client-decoded audio plays in stereo, through a decoder package that supports it. Other audio is unaffected.
WebGPUBrightnessHelp: Adds or removes display brightness after tone mapping.
WebGPUCenterLevelHelp: Scales the center channel contribution; values above 1 boost it.
WebGPUClearProbeCacheHelp: Clears this browser's saved decoder test results, so the next playback tests again, for example after a driver update.
WebGPUCrashedProbes: Decoder tests that crashed here, skipped until cleared: {0}
WebGPUContrastHelp: Scales display contrast after tone mapping.
WebGPUDownmixGainsHelp: Values above 1 amplify the selected contribution. Boosted multichannel stereo downmixes are peak-limited; the selected WebGPU downmix algorithm still controls the base matrix. Native-media audio and HTML fallback playback do not consume these settings.
WebGPUDownmixOutputGainHelp: Boosts the completed stereo downmix before peak limiting.
WebGPUEnableCustomDecodeHelp: When enabled, the player demuxes and decodes direct-play sources itself. When off, behavior reverts to native HTML video player.
WebGPUEnableGPUDecodeSlicingHelp: Submits decoder work to the GPU in slices, so the frame on screen waits behind less decoding - useful for low-end GPUs. It can drastically lower decode speed on fast GPUs. When off, each picture's work submits at once. Requires custom decode.
WebGPUEnableHDRToneMappingHelp: Enables tone mapping with WebGPU, using the settings below. When off, HDR plays natively where the browser supports it, and the server transcodes it to SDR otherwise. Requires custom decode.
WebGPUForceStereo: Force stereo for WebGPU client-decoded audio
WebGPUForceStereoHelp: Otherwise client-decoded surround audio can play to the speaker layout.
WebGPUHighlightDesaturationHelp: Reduces saturation near the brightest mapped values.
WebGPUManualInputPeakHelp: Manual HDR source peak used when metadata tracking is off.
WebGPUOutputPeakHelp: Peak luminance of the SDR output transform.
WebGPUPaperWhiteHelp: Reference white used by the HDR-to-SDR transform.
WebGPUPlaybackChangesRestartRequired: Playback changes are restart-required and apply after restarting playback or starting the next item.
WebGPUPlaybackChangesSavedStatus: Saved. Playback changes are restart-required and apply after restarting playback or starting the next item.
WebGPUPreferredVideoPlayerHelp: Selects the local player when a new video starts. The WebGPU player automatically falls back to HTML if its presentation or custom decoding path fails.
WebGPUProbeCacheClearedStatus: Cleared. The next playback tests this browser's decoders again.
WebGPURedetectAudioOutputHelp: Re-read the current output device and switch active audio to its speaker layout
WebGPURenderStatusInactive: Saved. Controls apply when an HDR-to-SDR WebGPU presentation is active.
WebGPURenderStatusPeakUnavailable: Saved. The detected source peak is unavailable; automatic tracking will apply to the next HDR presentation.
WebGPURenderStatusPending: Saved. The current presentation could not apply the change; it will apply to the next HDR presentation.
WebGPUSaturationHelp: Scales display saturation after tone mapping.
WebGPUSpeakerLayoutHelp: The speaker layout that WebGPU client-decoded audio plays to. Auto follows the channel count of the audio output, up to 7.1.4; 5.1.2 and 5.1.4 apply only when chosen. A layout wider than the output plays as Auto. Dolby Atmos fills every speaker of the layout when a decoder package renders its objects.
WebGPUSurroundLevelHelp: Scales back and side channel contributions; values above 1 boost them.
WebGPUTrackSourcePeakMetadataHelp: When enabled, valid stream metadata replaces the manual input peak.
WebGPUHDROutputHelp: Shows HDR video as HDR, mapped to the output peak and paper white set above, instead of tone mapping it to SDR. SDR video and SDR displays are unaffected.
WebGPUHDROutputApplied: HDR output saved. It applies to HDR video on an HDR display.
WebGPUHDROutputFailed: HDR output could not be applied: {0}
WebGPUBlackBarCropHelp: Finds the black bars encoded into the video while it plays and shows only the picture, which then fits the screen by its own shape, so a letterboxed film fills an ultrawide screen. A picture that grows into the bars, such as a film's IMAX scenes, shows whole at once.
WebGPUBlackBarCropApplied: Black bar crop saved. It shows on video with black bars, on a screen of another shape than the video's or with the Cover aspect mode.
WebGPUBlackBarCropFailed: Black bar crop could not be applied: {0}
WebGPUDeinterlaceDoubleRate: Double rate, a frame per field
WebGPUDeinterlaceSingleRate: Single rate, a frame per frame
WebGPUDeinterlaceHelp: How interlaced video that plays through WebGPU decode is shown. Double rate shows each field as a frame and keeps the motion of broadcast video; single rate halves it; off shows the frames woven, as decoded. Progressive video is unaffected.
WebGPUDeinterlaceApplied: Deinterlacing saved. It applies to interlaced video at once.
WebGPUShaderPassesHelp: WebGPU passes are WGSL shader files that run in the order listed, in this browser only. A file of several passes runs them in file order. Until you change the list, it shows the server's default passes.
WebGPUShaderPassesFailed: The WebGPU passes could not be applied: {0}
WebGPUShaderPassesStorageFailed: The shader files could not be stored: {0}
WebGPUSettingsSaveFailed: The settings could not be saved in this browser: {0}
WebGPUShaderPassFilesSkipped: Not added: {0}. A preset holds at most {1} files of at most {2} characters each.
WebGPUShaderPassParameterPending: Saved. It applies once the pass runs ({0}).
WebGPUServerPassesNone: The server offers no other passes.
WebGPUServerPassAdded: {0} downloaded from the server and added.
WebGPUShaderPassWithdrawn: From the server: {0}, which no longer offers it
WebGPUServerDecoders: The server offers {0}; each downloads when a playback needs it.
WebGPUDecoderPackagesHelp: A decoder package is one .wasm file that adds a video or audio decoder in this browser only, or replaces the server's package of its id. Your packages come first, and they may play without test vectors, so add only packages you trust. Changes apply from the next playback.
WebGPUDecoderPackageUnusable: Unusable, so playback leaves it out: {0}
WebGPUDecoderPackagesStorageFailed: The decoder packages could not be read or stored: {0}
WebGPUSettingsButtonPlacementHelp: Where the video player offers these settings: a button before or after its settings button, a button at the end of its controls, or an item of its settings menu. Applies at once.
WebGPUSettingsButtonPlacementControlsEnd: At the end of the controls
WebGPUPlayerRestartingPlayback: The current video restarts in the other player.
WebGPUPlayerCurrentVideoUnchanged: The current video keeps its player.
WebGPUPlayerAppliesNextPlayback: It applies from the next playback.
WebGPUClientDefaultsHelp: Reset to default restores the built-in value. Retroactively apply to clients saves, and also drops users' own choices of that setting.
WebGPUClientDefaultsApplied: Saved. Every client follows the default of {0} again.
WebGPUClientDefaultsShaderPassesHelp: The server's pass files users run, in the order listed, unless they choose their own; at most {0} files. Only parameter values that differ from a pass's default are stored.
WebGPUClientDefaultsShaderPassesFull: The list holds at most {0} files.
WebGPUClientDefaultsPassNotOffered: The server no longer offers this file, so users run the others without it.
WebGPUClientDefaultsPassUnreadable: Its parameters could not be read: {0}
WebGPUClientDefaultsReadFailed: The server's defaults could not be read: {0}
WebGPUClientDefaultsRefused: The server holds values users cannot take for: {0}. The form shows what users take instead.
WebGPUDecoderTestsHelp: Decoder tests check what a browser can play. In the background, they make the first playback start sooner; a device used only as a remote needs none. Changes apply at each client's next page load.
WebGPUDecoderTestTimingHelp: Users can override this in their WebGPU settings.
WebGPUDecoderTestTimingDialogHelp: In the background makes the first playback start sooner. By device type and rules follows the server's settings. Applies from the next page load.
WebGPUDecoderTestTimingBackground: In the background after the page loads
WebGPUDecoderTestTimingSavedStatus: Saved. It applies from the next page load.
WebGPUDecoderTestBackgroundDevices: Devices that run decoder tests in the background
WebGPUDecoderTestBackgroundDevicesHelp: Checked types test in the background, others at the start of playback. Jellyfin apps count as their device's type.
WebGPUDecoderTestRulesHelp: One rule per line, such as playback device: *iPhone*: background or playback, then client, device, version, or ua, a colon, and a pattern. * and ? are wildcards; # starts a comment. The first match wins, before device types. At most {0} rules and {1} characters.
WebGPUDecoderTestRuleSyntax: Line {0} is not a rule: background or playback, a field, a colon, and a pattern.
WebGPUDecoderTestRuleTiming: Line {0} starts with neither background nor playback.
WebGPUDecoderTestRuleField: Line {0} names a field other than client, device, version, or ua.
WebGPUDecoderTestRulePattern: Line {0} has no pattern after its colon.
WebGPUDecoderTestRuleTooMany: Line {0} is a rule past the limit of {1}.
WebGPUDecoderTestRulesTooLong: The rules hold {0} characters, more than the {1} allowed.
WebGPUDecoderTestRulesNotSaved: The defaults were not saved, since the decoder test rules have problems.
WebGPUNumberUncommitted: Press Enter to apply, or Escape to undo
WebGPUValueBeyondSlider: The value lies beyond the slider, which spans {0} to {1}
WebGPUPipelineGraphEmpty: The pipeline shows while a video plays through WebGPU.
WebGPUPipelineGraphSummary: Passes in order, from the source to the canvas: {0}.
WebGPUWindowMoveHelp: Drag the title, or press the arrow keys on it, to move the window; Shift moves it further. Enter collapses or expands it, Home returns it to its place in the windows' order, and Delete hides it.
WebGPUKeyboardShortcutsHelp:
Tab, Shift+Tab: next or previous control
F6, Shift+F6: next or previous window
1 to 9: show or hide the listed window
Arrow keys on a window's title: move the window; Shift moves it further
Enter on a window's title: collapse or expand it; Home: back to the first free place; Delete: hide it
Alt+R: restore the focused setting's default
Alt+I: show or hide the focused setting's details
Number fields: the arrow keys and Page Up and Page Down step the value at once; a typed value applies on Enter, and Escape undoes it
Escape: close the settings
WebGPUToneMapOperatorHelp: The curve that maps HDR brightness into SDR. Reinhard, the default, rolls highlights off gently; Spline works in a perceptual space and follows each scene's average brightness where HDR10+ or Dolby Vision metadata gives it; ACES gives a filmic look with stronger contrast; ST 2094-40 follows the tone curve a video's HDR10+ metadata carries, and matches each scene's brightness where there is none.
WebGPUShowFailureReportHelp: Opens the report of the last time WebGPU failed on this page, also while the warning is off. The button waits until WebGPU fails.
WebGPUFailureWarningSettingHelp: When WebGPU fails and a video plays through the browser's own video player instead, a window explains the likely cause and how to fix it, once per page load.
WebGPUFailureSummary: WebGPU failed, so this video plays through the browser's own video player. HDR tone mapping, WebGPU passes and the decoders that need WebGPU are off for it.
WebGPUFailureCopyHint: Web pages cannot open the browser's own pages: copy an address with its button and paste it into the address bar.
WebGPUFailureShowWarning: Show this warning when WebGPU fails
WebGPUFailureShowWarningSaveFailed: The choice could not be saved: {0}
WebGPUFailureReportCopyManual: This page may not copy: select the report below and copy it.
WebGPUFailureValueCopyFailed: This page may not copy {0}: select it and copy it yourself.
WebGPUFailureConfidenceLikely: This is the most likely cause; the browser's own pages named below tell for sure.
WebGPUFailureConfidencePossible: This is a guess from what the page can see; the steps below cover the usual causes.
WebGPUFailureCauseDeviceFailed: The GPU refused what the player needs
WebGPUFailureCauseDeviceLost: The GPU was lost during playback
WebGPUFailureCauseGPUBlocked: The browser has blocked this GPU or its driver
WebGPUFailureCauseInsecureContext: This page is not opened over HTTPS
WebGPUFailureCauseSoftwareRenderer: The browser is not using a real GPU
WebGPUFailureCauseWebGPUMissing: WebGPU is turned off in this browser
WebGPUFailureCauseWebGPUNotShipped: This browser has no WebGPU here yet
WebGPUFailureCauseInsecureContextHelp: This page was opened over plain HTTP ({0}). Browsers give WebGPU only to secure pages: ones opened over HTTPS, or from this computer itself (localhost).
WebGPUFailureCauseReleaseBuildHelp: {0} reported that its release builds do not have WebGPU on {1} yet. Firefox, and the browsers built on it, have it there only in Firefox Nightly so far.
WebGPUFailureCauseNotOnPlatformHelp: {0} does not have WebGPU on {1} yet. Firefox, and the browsers built on it such as Zen and LibreWolf, have it there only in test builds such as Firefox Nightly so far.
WebGPUFailureCauseFlagOnlyHelp: {0} on Windows on ARM has WebGPU only behind a flag so far.
WebGPUFailureCauseFirefoxIntelMacHelp: {0} has WebGPU on Macs with Apple Silicon only; on Intel Macs it is still limited to Firefox Nightly.
WebGPUFailureCauseSomeGPUsHelp: {0} on {1} turns WebGPU on only for some GPUs and drivers so far, and this one does not seem to be among them.
WebGPUFailureCauseTooOldHelp: {0} {1} is too old: it has WebGPU on this system from version {2}.
WebGPUFailureCauseSafariTooOldHelp: Safari {0} has WebGPU only behind a feature flag; it is on by default from Safari {1}, which comes with {2} {1}.
WebGPUFailureCauseWebGPUMissingHelp: {0} does not offer WebGPU to this page. A setting, a flag or a policy may have turned it off, or this version may not have it.
WebGPUFailureCauseWebGPUMissingChromiumH: {0} does not offer WebGPU to this page, although it has WebGPU on this system. A changed flag, an administrator's policy or hardware acceleration turned off may be the reason.
WebGPUFailureCauseWebGPUMissingFirefoxHe: {0} does not offer WebGPU to this page, although Firefox has it on this system, so its preference dom.webgpu.enabled is probably off. LibreWolf turns it off by default.
WebGPUFailureCauseWebGPUMissingSafariHel: {0} does not offer WebGPU to this page, although this version of Safari has it on by default. Safari's WebGPU feature flag may be off, or Lockdown Mode may turn it off.
WebGPUFailureCauseGPUCrashedHelp: The GPU device was lost on this page, and now {0} offers no GPU to WebGPU at all. After its graphics process crashes a few times, a browser keeps GPU features off until it restarts.
WebGPUFailureCauseAdapterTimeoutHelp: {0} did not answer a request for a GPU within a few seconds. Its graphics process may be stuck or have crashed.
WebGPUFailureCauseAdapterRejectedHelp: {0} refused the request for a GPU: {1}
WebGPUFailureCauseSoftwareRendererHelp: {0} draws with {1}, which is software rendering, not a real GPU. That happens over Remote Desktop, in a virtual machine, without a working GPU driver, or when hardware acceleration is off.
WebGPUFailureCauseFallbackAdapterHelp: {0} offers only a software WebGPU adapter, so no real GPU is in use. That happens over Remote Desktop, in a virtual machine, without a working GPU driver, or when hardware acceleration is off.
WebGPUFailureCauseHardwareAccelerationOf: {0} offers neither WebGPU nor WebGL to this page. That usually means its hardware acceleration setting is off, or it has turned GPU features off for this computer altogether.
WebGPUFailureCauseGPUBlockedHelp: {0} renders with {1}, but offers no WebGPU adapter for it. Browsers block WebGPU on GPUs and drivers with known problems, most often because the driver is out of date.
WebGPUFailureCauseGPUBlockedUnnamedHelp: {0} offers no WebGPU adapter to this page. Browsers block WebGPU on GPUs and drivers with known problems, most often because the driver is out of date; it is also off when hardware acceleration is off.
WebGPUFailureCauseNoAdapterHelp: {0} offers no WebGPU adapter to this page, and the page cannot tell why.
WebGPUFailureCauseDeviceLostHelp: The GPU device was lost during playback and could not be recovered. A GPU driver reset, a switch between GPUs, sleep, or a crash of {0}'s graphics process does that; WebGPU works again now, so it may have been a one-off.
WebGPUFailureCauseDeviceFailedHelp: The GPU was found, but refused the device the player asked for ({0}). The GPU or its driver may not support the limits the player needs.
WebGPUFailureCauseRenderingFailedHelp: WebGPU works, but drawing the video with it failed ({0}: {1}). This may be a problem of the browser, the GPU driver or the add-on.
WebGPUFailureCauseTransientHelp: WebGPU failed for this video, but {0} offers a GPU to WebGPU again now, so the failure may have been temporary.
WebGPUFailureStepCheckFirefoxSupport: To see what the browser itself says, open {0} and look at the {1} section, especially its WebGPU line and the {2}.
WebGPUFailureStepCheckGPUReport: To see what the browser itself says, open {0} and look at the {1} line and the {2} section. {3} saves that page to a file you can send along.
WebGPUFailureStepEnableHardwareAccelerat: Open {0}, under Performance uncheck {1}, check {2}, and restart {3}.
WebGPUFailureStepEnableUnsafeWebGPUFlag: Open {0}, set {1} to Enabled, and relaunch {2}. It turns WebGPU on where the browser does not support it yet, so it may be unstable.
WebGPUFailureStepEnableVulkanFlag: If that is not enough, also set {1} at {0} to Enabled.
WebGPUFailureStepFirefoxAndroid: Firefox on Android has WebGPU only in Firefox Beta and Nightly, after setting {1} to {2} in {0}. Otherwise use Chrome.
WebGPUFailureStepFirefoxEnablePreference: Open {0}, accept the warning, search for {1}, set it to {2}, and restart {3}.
WebGPUFailureStepFirefoxIgnoreBlocklist: As a last resort, set {1} to {2} in {0} to use a blocked GPU anyway; it can crash or draw wrongly.
WebGPUFailureStepFirefoxTroubleshootMode: If {0} runs in Troubleshoot Mode, restart it normally: Troubleshoot Mode turns hardware acceleration off.
WebGPUFailureStepIOSUsesWebKit: On iPhone and iPad, {0} runs on Safari's engine, so Safari's settings and the iOS version decide WebGPU.

WebGPUFailureStepLinuxCommandLine: If {0} still has no WebGPU, start it from a terminal with {1}.
WebGPUFailureStepReloadPage: Reload this page and play the video again.
WebGPUFailureStepReportProblem: If nothing here helps, use Copy report and send the report to whoever runs this server.
WebGPUFailureStepResetFlags: Open {0}, choose {1}, and relaunch: a changed flag, such as the ANGLE backend set to D3D11 WARP, can turn WebGPU or the GPU off.
WebGPUFailureStepRestartBrowser: Quit {0} completely, every window, and start it again: after its graphics process crashes, the browser keeps GPU features off until it restarts.
WebGPUFailureStepSafariFeatureFlagIOS: Open {0} (on iOS 17 and earlier {1}), turn on {2}, then close and reopen Safari.
WebGPUFailureStepSafariFeatureFlagMacOS: In {0}, check {1}; then in {2}, turn on {3} and restart Safari.
WebGPUFailureStepSafariLockdownMode: If Lockdown Mode is on, it may turn WebGPU off: exclude this website from it, or turn it off.
WebGPUFailureStepUpdateGPUDriver: Update the GPU driver, from the GPU maker's website or the system's updates. Browsers block old drivers with known problems.
WebGPUFailureStepUpdateSystem: Update to {0} {1} or later: Safari's WebGPU comes with the system.

WebGPUFailureStepUseRealGPU: Use the browser on the computer's own GPU: not over Remote Desktop, and not in a virtual machine without GPU passthrough.
